correctness.rationale: At AB-count level m, the exact state is (m-x,m-y,k-x-y) with \(x+y\le k\). Every still-unmatched rare vertex is selected by the first edge of each level \(m\ge4k\) with probability at least \(1/m\); a telescoping product and union bound yield \(kM/n\). At each rare match above level M, the dense endpoint A-probability differs from 1/2 by at most \(k/[4(M-k)]\); a common-uniform coupling over at most k rare matches yields \(k^2/[4(M-k)]\). If all rare vertices disappear, core matching leaves \(|k-2B_k|\) vertices. This proves the TV inequality and its asymptotic and binomial consequences; 165 finite exact checker assertions corroborate but are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A rare third class constitutes a natural structural perturbation of a perfectly greedy-matchable complete bipartite graph. The theorem quantifies how an asymptotically vanishing vertex fraction creates a nonzero terminal optimality loss, gives the entire law with explicit approximation for \(k=o(n^{1/3})\), and reveals a folded-normal growing-minority regime. Deterministic extrema, generic algorithmic ratios and the known density-level results do not provide this observable.
